The record affirmatively shows a subgroup regression and affirmatively shows that the only proposed monitoring is informal and lacks reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or disclosure language. That means the clean compliance case is not available. The best defensible packet therefore narrows the claim: certify based on overall readiness while explicitly preserving the subgroup limitation in the packet as a required disclosure, and avoid suggesting that the nine-week-old approval or informal monitoring note cures the documentation gap. Private launch pressure reinforces why velocity is being prioritized, but it is not admissible support and should not appear in the public justification.

Public governance guidance also supports certification when current evaluation results, limitations, and risk information are documented and monitored across deployment. The prior approval from nine weeks ago cannot substitute for current evidence, but it does provide context that this model family has previously cleared review.
